parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented police/border targeting of trans people, no facility or custody rule, and an independent human-rights report records no torture, arbitrary detention or abuses; discrimination is described as rare and courts do enforce hate-speech/hate-crime law (albeit on sexual-orientation grounds, with documented convictions). Against this: gender identity is absent from every protective provision, there is no anti-discrimination ban, no legal gender recognition, very low visibility, a socially conservative Catholic majority calling trans identity immoral, and a near-bottom regional rights ranking. That is social disapproval/potential service refusal with no remedy (tier 3 at most) — real, but undocumented as visitor-facing harm. With no universal-exposure measure and functioning institutions, this sits at the top of the Elevated band rather than in Reduced Risk, since no positive acceptance or working protection for trans visitors is documented.
